title: Why You Instantly Correct Other People's Small Mistakes
hook: Your brain has a secret mission: to fix everything.

narration.text: When someone makes a small speech error, you feel compelled to correct them.
This is your brain's language processing at work.
It constantly predicts what will be said next.
A mistake means the prediction was wrong.
Your brain automatically flags this as an error needing correction.
It is not rudeness, but an impulse to complete the linguistic puzzle.
Notice it next time someone mispronounces a word, it is a fascinating reflex.
Comment if you have ever done this, like this if it surprised you, subscribe for more brain insights, and share this with someone who always corrects.

description: Ever wonder why you automatically correct people when they make a small mistake in speech? It is not about being rude, it is about how your brain processes language.
topic: Why you automatically correct someone when they make a small mistake in speech. This is your brain's language processing at work.
